chunks: And from him, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Lu'lu'i, from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Fit'r ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said:

He said, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What befalls the months regarding deficiency (shortening to 29 days) also befalls the month of Ramadan. So when you fast the month of Ramadan for twenty-nine days, then if it is overcast (cloudy, preventing sighting), complete the count to thirty days.'
ai.seo_question: How do you determine if Ramadan is 29 or 30 days when the moon is not visible?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of the 'completing the count' (istikmal) rule when moon sighting is obstructed by clouds, a key mechanism in Shia lunar calendar jurisprudence. It underscores the flexibility within the Sharia to maintain the sanctity of the month even when astronomical visibility is hindered, ensuring the fast is not prematurely broken.
